scenarios: a managed device policy requires sandboxed execution, telemetry off, a proxy, trust roots and an update floor, and denies network egress
the repository's .modbit/config.json switches the sandbox and telemetry back and allows egress and execution; the user's configuration names its own proxy: every attempt is refused and recorded
GetEffectivePolicy shows the device constraints exactly as the device wrote them, their source path, and network.egress=DENY by Device
shell.exec under local_trusted is POLICY_DENIED / DEVICE_REQUIRES_SANDBOX and nothing runs

ci.note: every Rust job green on macOS, Linux and Windows; the Ubuntu desktop-E2E job passed on rerun after a quiet-hours clock race in states.spec (a follow-up task was raised)

audit: DOCUMENTED-ONLY for the device before: the kernel envelope doc named admin/device authority but the Core used the compiled default; configuration had no machine layer; a device key in any file was silently ignored.
proof: Real Core and terminal broker: the machine's managed policy stands above the organization, repository and user; their attempts to disable its requirements are refused on the record, and execution outside an isolated profile is refused.
negative_proof: The project's and user's device keys set nothing; the host-profile shell.exec starts no process.
limitations: Enforced: sandbox requirement and device permissions. Represented and shown, enforced by their owners later: proxy and trust roots (egress broker), update channel and floor (M10.2), telemetry (M10.1). No MDM profile format is parsed.
